ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The records use the bodily image for persons brought into exceptionally close conjunction: Liao’an Qingyu says that for five or six years he has had his brows intertwined with the assembly, yet in fact they have had "no traffic in rice or water" (五六年來雖則與諸人眉毛廝結，其實水米無交).
EvidenceBody: Another requires "brows intertwined, sharing life and sharing death" (眉毛廝結，同生同死). It also appears as an answer in a public interview: asked for the phrase for opening the retreat, Feiyin Tongrong replies, "brows intertwined" (眉毛廝結). Elsewhere a hall address sets saying and silence against each other: "if one speaks, heaven and earth are far apart; if one does not speak, brows are intertwined" (說即天地懸殊，不說即眉毛廝結). The Chan use turns a physical impossibility into a compact, repeatable encounter phrase; the accompanying clauses establish proximity or conjunction but do not authorize this entry to decide what speakers intend by it.
